fields.name: minor_units
fields.doc:
MinorUnits is the number of decimal places. Required for a new
currency; a built-in one keeps its own.

fields.name: grouping
fields.doc: Grouping is thousands (default), indian (12,34,567) or none.

fields.name: database
fields.doc: Database names the database.sql resource; Table defaults to the name.

fields.name: path
fields.doc:
Path is the collection URL (default /api/<name>s). Auth names the
authenticator for its routes; AllowAnonymous makes auth optional.

block.doc: EntityColumn is one field of an entity.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc:
Kind: text (default), integer, number, decimal, boolean, date,
datetime, email, json. A decimal (money) is exact: stored as integer
minor units with Scale decimals (default 2) and returned as a string
such as "1250.50".

fields.name: read_only
currency
fields.doc:
Currency makes a decimal column a money column: its scale is the
currency's minor units (2 for NPR, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD). The kind
defaults to decimal.

fields.name: tenant_scoped
fields.doc:
TenantScoped stamps and filters tenant_id; OwnerScoped limits every
operation to rows the caller created unless they hold OwnerBypassRoles.

fields.name: org_resource
fields.doc:
OrgResource (org.hierarchy) + OrgColumn scope rows to the caller's
organisational units.

fields.name: versioned
fields.doc:
Versioned adds a version column; updates must send the version they
read and get 409 when it moved.

fields.name: search
fields.doc: Search lists text columns ?q= matches (case-insensitive substring).

fields.name: search_index
fields.doc:
SearchIndex keeps a token index of the Search columns (lower-cased,
accent-folded words in <table>_search), written in each change's
transaction; ?q= then matches every query word as a word prefix.

fields.name: analytics
fields.doc:
Analytics enables GET {path}/-/analytics: several metrics, up to two
group-by columns and a day/week/month time bucket in one call.

fields.name: bulk
fields.doc:
Bulk enables POST {path}/-/bulk: many creates, updates and deletes in
one request, all-or-nothing by default; BulkMax caps its items
(default 500).

fields.name: migrate
fields.doc: Migrate creates the table and indexes at startup (default true).

block.doc:
EntityAccess allows an operation: list, get, create, update, delete,
export, aggregate, analytics or "*" (the default for ops without their own blocks —
an op's own blocks replace it). Roles restrict it to role holders; Condition is
checked against the record (and principal) for get/update/delete and
against the submitted record for create.

EntityHook runs an intent after a committed change: created, updated,
deleted or "*".

A durable hook is recorded in the same transaction as the change and
delivered by a background dispatcher with retries (MaxAttempts, default
10; RetryBase doubling, default 2s) and dead-lettering, so it survives a
crash and a failing downstream. Delivery is at-least-once: its input
carries a stable event_id for idempotency.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Default is the value when no rule matches (default false).

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc: Disabled forces the default for everyone (a kill switch in BCL).

fields.name: rule
fields.doc: Rules are tried in order; the first that matches decides.

block.doc: FlagRule targets a slice of callers. Every criterion set must match.

fields.name: rollout
fields.doc:
Rollout admits this percentage (0-100) of matching callers, stably by
user (or tenant when anonymous).

fields.name: variant
fields.doc: Variant picks one of the flag's variants instead of Value.

fields.name: variant
fields.doc: Variants split callers by weight when no rule matched (A/B tests).

block.doc: FlagVariant is one arm of an experiment.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: Value defaults to the variant name.

intent.name: intent
intent.doc:
IntentSpec describes one REF dependency graph and the resource budget it may
spend. An intent is the request-scoped unit of work: it is compiled into an
immutable plan whose producers are proven, whose cycles are rejected, and
whose independent nodes run concurrently.

An intent has no control flow of its own — every node in its plan runs, gated
only by policy decisions and speculation class. Conditionals, loops, races
and retries are expressed with the flow.* actions, which invoke child intents
from inside a single node (see flow.go). Anything that must survive a process
restart belongs in a ProcessSpec instead.

fields.name: response
fields.doc: Response names the fact whose value becomes the intent's result.

fields.name: input_schema
fields.doc:
InputSchema names a schema block validated against the decoded input
before any node runs. This is the cheapest place to reject bad input:
nothing has been read, written or spent yet.

fields.name: output_schema
fields.doc:
OutputSchema validates the response fact, catching a graph that quietly
stopped producing a field its consumers depend on.

fields.name: authz
fields.doc:
Authz gates the whole intent. It is enforced as a REF decision node, so
it participates in the deny-dominant decision algebra and blocks every
effect node in the plan rather than being advisory.

block.doc:
AuthzSpec is one authorization gate, used identically on a route, an intent,
an intent node and a process step. One shape, one evaluation order, so a
reviewer reads the same rules everywhere.

Evaluation order is fixed and deny-dominant:

 1. DenyRoles   — holding any listed role denies, immediately
 2. Roles       — must hold at least one (or all, when RequireAll)
 3. Permissions — must hold every listed permission
 4. Condition   — must evaluate true

An empty AuthzSpec denies rather than allows. A gate that was written but
left unfilled is a mistake, and the safe reading of a mistake is "no".

fields.name: require_all
fields.doc: RequireAll makes Roles conjunctive instead of disjunctive.

fields.name: scopes
fields.doc: Scopes requires OAuth-style scopes, checked like Permissions.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc:
Condition is an expression over principal, tenant, input, session and
the facts available at this point — the hook for ownership checks such
as "principal.id == input.owner_id".

fields.name: authorizer
fields.doc:
Authorizer names an authz resource. Empty uses the application's single
authorizer; naming one matters only in a deployment with several.

fields.name: on_deny
fields.doc:
OnDeny is "error" (default, 403), "skip" (node/step only: publish
Fallback and continue) or "redirect:<step>" (process steps only).

fields.name: message
fields.doc:
Message overrides the denial text shown to the caller. Keep it vague:
a precise denial reason is an information leak about what exists.

fields.name: idempotent
fields.doc:
Idempotent marks an intent safe to replay with the same input. Route and
worker idempotency guards refuse to short-circuit a non-idempotent
intent, so a replayed POST cannot silently return a cached success for
work that actually needs doing again.

fields.name: input_data
fields.doc:
InputData and OutputData shape the intent's boundaries: InputData rewrites
the decoded request before it is published as the "input" fact, OutputData
shapes the response fact on the way out (redaction, field masking,
renames for a public API contract).

block.doc:
DataSpec is the declarative payload-shaping pipeline, applied wherever data
crosses a boundary: an intent's input and output, a node's inputs and
outputs, a process edge's payload, a route's response.

The stages run in a fixed, documented order so the same spec always produces
the same result regardless of how it was written:

 1. Source      — narrow to a sub-path of the incoming value
 2. Defaults    — fill absent keys
 3. Extract     — build target keys from expressions over the input
 4. Set         — assign literal or templated values
 5. Transforms  — per-path operations, in declaration order
 6. Append/Prepend — string and list concatenation
 7. Rename      — move keys
 8. Coerce      — convert types
 9. Flatten     — lift nested objects into the parent
 10. Pick/Omit  — select the surviving key set
 11. Redact/Mask — remove or partially hide sensitive values
 12. Filters    — accept or reject the whole payload
 13. Limits     — enforce MaxBytes and MaxDepth
 14. Schema     — structural validation, last, on the final shape

Every stage is optional. A zero DataSpec is a no-op and costs nothing: the
compiler omits the pipeline entirely rather than running fourteen empty
stages per request.

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
Source narrows the incoming value to one path before anything else runs,
e.g. "order.customer".

fields.name: extract
fields.doc:
Extract builds output keys from expressions evaluated over the input:
extract { total "order.amount * order.quantity" }. The target key may be
dotted to build nested output.

fields.name: set
fields.doc:
Set assigns literal values. String values support {{ }} templating over
the same variable environment as expressions.

fields.name: defaults
fields.doc:
Defaults fill keys that are absent or null, never keys that are present
and empty — "" and 0 are values, not absences.

fields.name: pick
fields.doc:
Pick keeps only these keys (dotted paths allowed); Omit removes these.
When both are set Pick runs first.

fields.name: rename
fields.doc: Rename moves keys: rename { customer_id "customerId" }.

fields.name: coerce
fields.doc:
Coerce converts values in place: coerce { amount "float" age "int" }.
Supported targets are string, int, float, bool, time, duration, json.

fields.name: append
fields.doc: Append and Prepend concatenate onto an existing string or list value.

fields.name: flatten
fields.doc:
Flatten lifts the named nested objects' keys into the parent and removes
the nesting, e.g. flatten [address] turns address.city into city.

fields.name: redact
fields.doc:
Redact removes these paths entirely. Mask replaces them with a fixed
number of asterisks plus the last few characters, so a support agent can
still recognise a value without being able to read it.

fields.name: mask_keep
fields.doc: MaskKeep is how many trailing characters Mask preserves. Default 4.

block.doc:
DataTransformSpec is one per-path operation inside a DataSpec.

Either Expr (an expression whose result replaces the value at Path) or Op
(a named operation, optionally parameterised by Arg) must be set. Named ops
are the common cases that would otherwise need an awkward expression:
upper, lower, trim, title, slug, hash, base64, base64_decode, json_encode,
json_decode, round, abs, length, first, last, unique, sort, join, split,
now, timestamp, uuid, default.

fields.name: only_if
fields.doc:
OnlyIf gates the transform on an expression, so one spec can shape
conditionally without a branch node.

block.doc:
DataFilterSpec accepts or rejects a whole payload.

Mode is "allow" (the default: the payload proceeds only when Expr is true) or
"deny" (the payload is rejected when Expr is true). A filtered payload on an
intent boundary is an invalid-input failure; on a process edge it means the
edge does not traverse, which is how DAGFlow's filter edges behave.

fields.name: max_bytes
fields.doc:
MaxBytes and MaxDepth bound the payload after shaping. They are a real
safety limit, not a hint: exceeding either fails the boundary rather
than truncating, because silently truncated data is worse than a refusal.

fields.name: strict
fields.doc:
Strict rejects the payload when Extract or Transforms reference a path
that does not exist, instead of treating it as null. Turn it on for
anything whose correctness depends on the field being there.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc: Schema names a schema block validated against the final shape.

block.doc:
NodeSpec describes one graph node. Requires and Provides are logical fact
names local to the containing intent: the compiler resolves them to dense
plan slots and proves that exactly one node produces each.

Type is catalog metadata (which family this node belongs to, for an editor);
Uses is the executable, versionable capability that actually runs. Kind and
Speculation are the REF safety declarations — they decide when the scheduler
is allowed to run this node relative to authentication and policy.

fields.name: family
fields.doc:
Family is catalog metadata: which semantic family this node belongs to.
BCL cannot bind a field named `type`, so it is spelled `family`.

fields.name: resource
fields.doc: Resource names the resource this node's action operates on, if any.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc:
Kind is the REF node kind: pure, read, decision, effect, async_effect or
stream. It determines whether the node runs before or after the effect
barrier, and whether a policy denial can stop it.

fields.name: speculation
fields.doc:
Speculation is the REF speculation class: none, pre_auth_safe,
post_identity_safe or post_policy_safe. The compiler proves the claim
against the graph and refuses a node that cannot honour it.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Description is carried into the catalog for editors and generated docs.

fields.name: input_data
fields.doc:
InputData reshapes the assembled Requires map before the action sees it;
OutputData reshapes what the action published before it becomes a fact.
Together they let one reusable action serve differently-shaped graphs
without a bespoke adapter node.

Retry retries this node in place. It is request-scoped: use a process
step's retry policy for anything that must survive a restart.

block.doc:
RetrySpec is one retry policy, shared by intent nodes and process steps.

Strategy is "fixed", "linear", "exponential", "exponential_jitter" or
"decorrelated_jitter". Jitter is applied on top of any strategy when set,
which matters for a dependency many replicas hit at once.

fields.name: retry_on
fields.doc:
RetryOn restricts retries to these failure categories (invalid_input,
not_found, conflict, permission, auth, rate_limit, unavailable, timeout,
internal). Empty means retry only the transient categories — never
invalid_input or permission, which will fail identically forever.

fields.name: timeout
fields.doc: Timeout bounds this node alone, inside the intent's own budget.

fields.name: bulkhead
fields.doc:
Bulkhead caps how many concurrent calls this node (or every node sharing
its Name) may have in flight, so a slow or flaky dependency cannot
exhaust every worker goroutine. It is the BCL-declarable equivalent of
capability.WithBulkhead, without requiring Go code.

of intents that share Name share one limiter, so a single flaky dependency
hit from several intents is capped once, in one place.

fields.doc:
Name identifies the shared limiter. Defaults to the node's own name
(scoped to its intent) when empty, so an unnamed bulkhead is private to
that one node.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc:
Limit is the maximum number of concurrent calls admitted. Required,
must be at least 1.

fields.doc:

when one graph serves several audiences and only part of it is
privileged.

review and a confirmation token, and only a second request carrying
the token takes the action.

fields.doc:

the default) or approved (the last approved version).

fields.name: approvals
fields.doc:

restricts who counts. Node names the gate node (default "gate").

matching none gets DefaultPriority and DefaultQueue.

case). When is an alias of it.

fields.doc: Priority orders work lists: 1 is the most urgent.

fields.name: roles
fields.doc:

urgent work) when the stage routes automatically.

fields.name: percent
fields.doc:
Percent (sampling) of cases, chosen deterministically from a hash of
the case id (and Salt), require human review; so do cases matching
SampleIf and, whatever the sample, AlwaysReviewIf. The rest pass
without review.

fields.name: confirm_submit

the first submit validates and returns a review with a confirmation
token, the second (with the token) commits.

fields.name: to
fields.doc:
To names recipients: assignee, previous_assignee, applicant, actor,
role:<role> (every directory worker holding it) or a user id.

fields.name: channels
fields.doc:
Channels are delivered by default; a recipient may opt out of them, or
into the host's other channels, per event.

fields.name: severity
fields.doc: Severity: info (default), warning, urgent or critical.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc:
Subject and Body are templates: {event}, {stage}, {actor},
{case.number}, {case.id}, {case.status} and {data.<form>.<input>}.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc:
Condition must hold for the rule to fire; the environment is the case
plus event {name, stage, actor, detail}. When is an alias of it.

process.name: process
process.doc:
ProcessSpec describes one durable, long-running orchestration: a persisted
state machine whose steps invoke intents and whose edges carry explicit
traversal semantics.

A process is what an intent cannot be. An intent lives and dies inside one
request; a process run is a row. It parks on a timer, an external event, a
manual gate or a human task; it survives a deploy, a crash and a replica
rescheduling; it compensates already-committed work when a later step fails.
Those semantics need persisted state, leases and optimistic versions — which
is why they are a separate tier rather than extra labels on REF's
dependency edges.

fields.name: store
fields.doc:
Store names a process-store resource (store.sql or store.file). It holds
runs, step states, timers, event subscriptions, joins, leases and human
tasks.

fields.name: queue
fields.doc:
Queue names the durable queue that carries advance work. Without it a run
can only be advanced in-process by the caller, which is fine for tests
and wrong for production — the compiler warns by requiring it for any
process that declares a timer, wait_event or human task.

fields.name: start
fields.doc:
Start names the first step. Required: a process with no entry point is a
configuration error, not an empty process.

fields.name: version
fields.doc:
Version lets a deployment decide what happens to runs started by an
earlier definition. See MigrationPolicy.

fields.name: migration_policy
fields.doc:
MigrationPolicy is "pin" (default: an in-flight run keeps executing the
definition it started on), "migrate" (adopt the new definition at the
next step boundary) or "fail" (refuse to advance and surface the run for
an operator). "pin" is the default because silently migrating a run
through a redesigned graph is how money goes missing.

fields.name: timeout
fields.doc:
Timeout bounds one whole run. MaxSteps bounds total step executions,
which is the backstop against a loop_until edge that never converges.

fields.name: max_visits
fields.doc: MaxVisits caps how many times any single step may execute in one run.

fields.name: idempotency
fields.doc:
Idempotency names the input path whose value deduplicates run creation,
e.g. "order.id". Starting twice with the same key returns the existing
run instead of creating a second one.

fields.name: retry
fields.doc:
Retry is the default retry policy for every step that does not set its
own. Unlike an intent node's retry, these attempts are persisted and
survive a restart.

block.doc:
RetrySpec is one retry policy, shared by intent nodes and process steps.

Strategy is "fixed", "linear", "exponential", "exponential_jitter" or
"decorrelated_jitter". Jitter is applied on top of any strategy when set,
which matters for a dependency many replicas hit at once.

fields.name: retry_on
fields.doc:
RetryOn restricts retries to these failure categories (invalid_input,
not_found, conflict, permission, auth, rate_limit, unavailable, timeout,
internal). Empty means retry only the transient categories — never
invalid_input or permission, which will fail identically forever.

fields.name: sla
fields.doc: SLA declares when a run is late and what to do about it.

block.doc: SLASpec declares when work is late and what happens then.

fields.name: target
fields.doc:
Target is the intended duration; Breach is when it is definitively late.
Between the two a run is "at risk", which is what an operations dashboard
wants to show before anything has actually failed.

fields.name: on_breach
fields.doc: OnBreach is "notify" (default), "escalate", "cancel" or "fail".

fields.name: notify
fields.doc: Notify names a notification channel resource.

fields.name: escalate
fields.doc: Escalate names the role a breached run's tasks are reassigned to.

fields.name: business_hours
fields.doc:
BusinessHours restricts elapsed-time accounting to working hours, so a
4-hour SLA raised on Friday evening is not breached by Monday morning.
Format is "Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00" with an optional trailing timezone.

fields.name: concurrency
fields.doc:
Concurrency caps simultaneously advancing runs of this process across the
whole deployment, enforced through the store's leases. Use it to protect
a downstream dependency that cannot take the full fan-out.

fields.name: retention
fields.doc:
Retention removes terminal runs after this age. Zero keeps them forever,
which is a deliberate choice an operator should make rather than a
default that quietly grows a table without bound.

block.doc:
DataSpec is the declarative payload-shaping pipeline, applied wherever data
crosses a boundary: an intent's input and output, a node's inputs and
outputs, a process edge's payload, a route's response.

The stages run in a fixed, documented order so the same spec always produces
the same result regardless of how it was written:

 1. Source      — narrow to a sub-path of the incoming value
 2. Defaults    — fill absent keys
 3. Extract     — build target keys from expressions over the input
 4. Set         — assign literal or templated values
 5. Transforms  — per-path operations, in declaration order
 6. Append/Prepend — string and list concatenation
 7. Rename      — move keys
 8. Coerce      — convert types
 9. Flatten     — lift nested objects into the parent
 10. Pick/Omit  — select the surviving key set
 11. Redact/Mask — remove or partially hide sensitive values
 12. Filters    — accept or reject the whole payload
 13. Limits     — enforce MaxBytes and MaxDepth
 14. Schema     — structural validation, last, on the final shape

Every stage is optional. A zero DataSpec is a no-op and costs nothing: the
compiler omits the pipeline entirely rather than running fourteen empty
stages per request.

fields.name: source
fields.doc:
Source narrows the incoming value to one path before anything else runs,
e.g. "order.customer".

fields.name: extract
fields.doc:
Extract builds output keys from expressions evaluated over the input:
extract { total "order.amount * order.quantity" }. The target key may be
dotted to build nested output.

fields.name: set
fields.doc:
Set assigns literal values. String values support {{ }} templating over
the same variable environment as expressions.

fields.name: defaults
fields.doc:
Defaults fill keys that are absent or null, never keys that are present
and empty — "" and 0 are values, not absences.

fields.name: pick
fields.doc:
Pick keeps only these keys (dotted paths allowed); Omit removes these.
When both are set Pick runs first.

fields.name: rename
fields.doc: Rename moves keys: rename { customer_id "customerId" }.

fields.name: coerce
fields.doc:
Coerce converts values in place: coerce { amount "float" age "int" }.
Supported targets are string, int, float, bool, time, duration, json.

fields.name: append
fields.doc: Append and Prepend concatenate onto an existing string or list value.

fields.name: flatten
fields.doc:
Flatten lifts the named nested objects' keys into the parent and removes
the nesting, e.g. flatten [address] turns address.city into city.

fields.name: redact
fields.doc:
Redact removes these paths entirely. Mask replaces them with a fixed
number of asterisks plus the last few characters, so a support agent can
still recognise a value without being able to read it.

fields.name: mask_keep
fields.doc: MaskKeep is how many trailing characters Mask preserves. Default 4.

block.doc:
DataTransformSpec is one per-path operation inside a DataSpec.

Either Expr (an expression whose result replaces the value at Path) or Op
(a named operation, optionally parameterised by Arg) must be set. Named ops
are the common cases that would otherwise need an awkward expression:
upper, lower, trim, title, slug, hash, base64, base64_decode, json_encode,
json_decode, round, abs, length, first, last, unique, sort, join, split,
now, timestamp, uuid, default.

fields.name: only_if
fields.doc:
OnlyIf gates the transform on an expression, so one spec can shape
conditionally without a branch node.

block.doc:
DataFilterSpec accepts or rejects a whole payload.

Mode is "allow" (the default: the payload proceeds only when Expr is true) or
"deny" (the payload is rejected when Expr is true). A filtered payload on an
intent boundary is an invalid-input failure; on a process edge it means the
edge does not traverse, which is how DAGFlow's filter edges behave.

fields.name: max_bytes
fields.doc:
MaxBytes and MaxDepth bound the payload after shaping. They are a real
safety limit, not a hint: exceeding either fails the boundary rather
than truncating, because silently truncated data is worse than a refusal.

fields.name: strict
fields.doc:
Strict rejects the payload when Extract or Transforms reference a path
that does not exist, instead of treating it as null. Turn it on for
anything whose correctness depends on the field being there.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc: Schema names a schema block validated against the final shape.

resource and action available to a request is available to a process — there
is no second, weaker action catalog to learn.

fields.name: process
fields.doc:
Process, when set instead of Intent, runs a child process as a sub-run.
The parent parks until the child reaches a terminal state.

fields.name: family
fields.doc:
Family is catalog metadata for an editor, mirroring NodeSpec.Family. BCL
cannot bind a field named `type`.

which matters for a dependency many replicas hit at once.

appears in the task list until somebody completes it.

instead; Strategy then decides who inside that group gets it.

fields.doc:

fields.name: reminder

fields.doc:

fields.name: allow_reassign

it, unless OnDeny says otherwise.

reviewer reads the same rules everywhere.

 1. DenyRoles   — holding any listed role denies, immediately
 2. Roles       — must hold at least one (or all, when RequireAll)
 3. Permissions — must hold every listed permission
 4. Condition   — must evaluate true

left unfilled is a mistake, and the safe reading of a mistake is "no".

fields.name: require_all
fields.doc: RequireAll makes Roles conjunctive instead of disjunctive.

fields.name: scopes
fields.doc: Scopes requires OAuth-style scopes, checked like Permissions.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc:

the facts available at this point — the hook for ownership checks such

fields.name: authorizer
fields.doc:

fields.name: on_deny
fields.doc:

Fallback and continue) or "redirect:<step>" (process steps only).

a precise denial reason is an information leak about what exists.

that must not run concurrently with itself across runs (adjusting shared
inventory, say) holds a real lease while it does.

this step may execute. When the limit is hit the run parks and retries
rather than failing, because a rate limit is backpressure, not an error.

block.doc:
EdgeSpec is one durable transition between steps. Its Type carries the
traversal semantics; every type is listed in the edge-type catalog and
implemented by ref/process.

Conditions: every edge type, without exception, evaluates When and Condition
before it traverses. They are two names for the same check — When reads
better for a guard, Condition for a data test — and both must pass. This is
one contract across all edge types so a fan-out or manual edge cannot bypass
a guard that a simple edge would honour.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc:
Kind is the edge type. BCL cannot bind a field named `type`, so the
traversal semantic is spelled `kind`.

fields.name: from
fields.doc:
From/To are the single-source, single-target form. Sources/Targets are
the multi form used by fan-in, fan-out, parallel, race and quorum.

fields.name: condition
fields.doc:
Condition must hold for the edge to traverse. Every edge type evaluates it,
without exception. When is an alias of it (BCL binds `when` since v0.0.34).

fields.name: strategy
fields.doc:
Strategy selects the completion rule for fan-in, join and quorum edges:
"all" (default), "any", "quorum", "partial_success" or "best_score".

fields.name: quorum
fields.doc:
Quorum is how many sources must complete for a quorum strategy. Zero
means a simple majority of Sources.

fields.name: max_concurrency
fields.doc:
MaxConcurrency bounds simultaneous targets for parallel and fan-out
edges, and is the cycle cap for loop_until.

fields.name: fail_fast
fields.doc: FailFast cancels sibling branches as soon as one fails.

fields.name: continue_on_error
fields.doc:
ContinueOnError keeps traversing when a branch fails, collecting the
error instead of failing the run.

fields.name: cancel_losers
fields.doc:
CancelLosers cancels the losing branches of a race once a winner is
known. Leave it off when the losers have side effects worth completing.

fields.name: timeout
fields.doc:
Timeout means different things per type, each documented in the edge
catalog: the park duration for delayed, the deadline for timeout and
wait_event, the backoff for retry, the spacing for rate_limited.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc: Attempts is the retry count for a retry edge.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: Event is the external event name a wait_event edge waits for.

fields.name: correlation
fields.doc:
Correlation is an expression producing the key that matches an inbound
event to this waiting run, e.g. "run.input.order_id".

fields.name: on_timeout
fields.doc:
OnTimeout names the step to go to when a wait_event or timeout edge
expires. Without it, expiry fails the run.

fields.name: weight
fields.doc:
Weight is the relative share of a weighted edge; Priority selects the
winner among priority edges (lowest value wins).

fields.name: rate_limit
fields.doc:
RateLimit names a rate-limiter resource for a rate_limited edge, with
Limit and Window. A rate_limited edge parks the run until the window
admits it; it never sleeps a worker thread.

fields.doc:

to the source step's result. BatchSize groups a batch_iterator.

fields.name: targets_path
fields.doc: TargetsPath is where a dynamic_fanout edge reads its runtime target list.

fields.name: threshold
fields.doc:
Thresholds route by numeric range for a threshold edge. The first rule
whose bounds contain the value wins.

block.doc:

inclusive, Max exclusive, and either may be omitted for an open bound.

fields.doc:

and why, rather than inferring it from the path taken.

fields.name: escalate
fields.doc: Escalate names the role an escalation edge reassigns work to.

fields.name: notify
fields.doc: Notify names a channel an escalation edge notifies.

fields.doc:

whether the edge traverses at all, which is how a filter edge works.

factory's own schema.

every node that names it, so connection pools, caches and queue consumers
have generation lifetime rather than request lifetime.

dependency the compiler cannot infer from a well-known config key.

the rest listed in resourceDependencyKeys) need no declaration.

inherits. The authz.rbac resource resolves the transitive closure once at
load time, so a permission check is a map lookup rather than a graph walk.

rejected at compile time.

Everything declared here is enforced before the intent is dispatched and
fails closed: an authz block that cannot resolve its authorizer, a rate-limit
block whose limiter is unreachable, or a tenant block that cannot determine a
tenant all refuse the request rather than letting it through unguarded.

fields.doc: Process starts a durable process run instead of dispatching an intent.

fields.doc:

(server-sent events) or "download" (stream a stored object).

fields.doc:

before dispatch and commits it after, so session nodes have one to use.

fields.doc:

resolved before dispatch and exposed to every node — so a node does not
have to re-derive identity, and an unauthenticated request never reaches
a graph that assumed one.

fields.doc:

names an authenticator, for endpoints like login that must be reachable
without credentials. It must be explicit: forgetting to set it fails
closed, forgetting to unset it does not silently open the route.

DataSpec is the declarative payload-shaping pipeline, applied wherever data
crosses a boundary: an intent's input and output, a node's inputs and
outputs, a process edge's payload, a route's response.

The stages run in a fixed, documented order so the same spec always produces
the same result regardless of how it was written:

 4. Set         — assign literal or templated values
 5. Transforms  — per-path operations, in declaration order
 6. Append/Prepend — string and list concatenation
 7. Rename      — move keys
 8. Coerce      — convert types
 9. Flatten     — lift nested objects into the parent
 10. Pick/Omit  — select the surviving key set
 11. Redact/Mask — remove or partially hide sensitive values
 12. Filters    — accept or reject the whole payload
 13. Limits     — enforce MaxBytes and MaxDepth

compiler omits the pipeline entirely rather than running fourteen empty
stages per request.

fields.doc:
Source narrows the incoming value to one path before anything else runs,
e.g. "order.customer".

fields.name: extract
fields.doc:
Extract builds output keys from expressions evaluated over the input:
extract { total "order.amount * order.quantity" }. The target key may be
dotted to build nested output.

fields.name: set
fields.doc:
Set assigns literal values. String values support {{ }} templating over
the same variable environment as expressions.

fields.name: defaults
fields.doc:
Defaults fill keys that are absent or null, never keys that are present
and empty — "" and 0 are values, not absences.

fields.name: pick
fields.doc:
Pick keeps only these keys (dotted paths allowed); Omit removes these.
When both are set Pick runs first.

fields.name: rename
fields.doc: Rename moves keys: rename { customer_id "customerId" }.

fields.name: coerce
fields.doc:
Coerce converts values in place: coerce { amount "float" age "int" }.
Supported targets are string, int, float, bool, time, duration, json.

fields.name: append
fields.doc: Append and Prepend concatenate onto an existing string or list value.

fields.name: flatten
fields.doc:
Flatten lifts the named nested objects' keys into the parent and removes
the nesting, e.g. flatten [address] turns address.city into city.

fields.name: redact
fields.doc:
Redact removes these paths entirely. Mask replaces them with a fixed
number of asterisks plus the last few characters, so a support agent can
still recognise a value without being able to read it.

fields.name: mask_keep
fields.doc: MaskKeep is how many trailing characters Mask preserves. Default 4.

DataTransformSpec is one per-path operation inside a DataSpec.

Either Expr (an expression whose result replaces the value at Path) or Op
(a named operation, optionally parameterised by Arg) must be set. Named ops
are the common cases that would otherwise need an awkward expression:
upper, lower, trim, title, slug, hash, base64, base64_decode, json_encode,
json_decode, round, abs, length, first, last, unique, sort, join, split,
now, timestamp, uuid, default.

fields.name: only_if
fields.doc:
OnlyIf gates the transform on an expression, so one spec can shape
conditionally without a branch node.

block.doc:
DataFilterSpec accepts or rejects a whole payload.

Mode is "allow" (the default: the payload proceeds only when Expr is true) or
"deny" (the payload is rejected when Expr is true). A filtered payload on an
intent boundary is an invalid-input failure; on a process edge it means the
edge does not traverse, which is how DAGFlow's filter edges behave.

fields.name: max_bytes
fields.doc:
MaxBytes and MaxDepth bound the payload after shaping. They are a real
safety limit, not a hint: exceeding either fails the boundary rather
than truncating, because silently truncated data is worse than a refusal.

fields.name: strict
fields.doc:
Strict rejects the payload when Extract or Transforms reference a path
that does not exist, instead of treating it as null. Turn it on for
anything whose correctness depends on the field being there.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc: Schema names a schema block validated against the final shape.

block.doc:
SecurityEventSpec reports this route's outcome to the document's
security.tcpguard resource (if one is declared), after the response is
known — OnSuccess when the final status is < 400, OnFailure otherwise.
Either may be left empty to report only one direction.

This exists because the guard's own automatic per-request check
(routes.go's serve, before dispatch) only ever sees "request.received":
at that point in the pipeline, whether a login attempt will succeed is
not yet decided. A rule keyed on an *outcome* — auth-abuse-velocity's
abuse.auth.ip_failures, account-takeover's session drift, anything
needing "did this attempt fail" — cannot fire without something telling
the guard that outcome after the fact, which is what this does.

	route "auth.login" {
	  ...
	  security_event { on_success "auth.login_success" on_failure "auth.login_failed" }
	}

route_group.name: route_group
route_group.doc:
RouteGroupSpec batches routes that share a path prefix and, optionally, a
session/auth/authz/rate-limit default. It exists purely as an authoring
convenience: expandRouteGroups (route_group.go) turns each nested route
into an ordinary RouteSpec before compilation, so nothing downstream of it
— the planner, the validator, the mounter — knows groups ever existed.

A nested route's own Session/Auth/Authz/RateLimit/CacheControl/Tags win
over the group's when both are set; the group only fills in what a route
left empty. AllowAnonymous is the one field a nested route must set for
itself when it needs it (e.g. a login route inside an otherwise
authenticated group) — it is never inherited, so a group can never make a
route more open than the route itself asked to be.

RouteSpec projects an intent or a process onto HTTP.

Everything declared here is enforced before the intent is dispatched and
fails closed: an authz block that cannot resolve its authorizer, a rate-limit
block whose limiter is unreachable, or a tenant block that cannot determine a
tenant all refuse the request rather than letting it through unguarded.

fields.doc: Process starts a durable process run instead of dispatching an intent.

fields.name: mode
fields.doc:
Mode is "sync" (default), "async" (enqueue and return 202), "stream"
(server-sent events) or "download" (stream a stored object).

fields.doc:
Session names a session resource. When set, the route begins a session
before dispatch and commits it after, so session nodes have one to use.

fields.name: auth
fields.doc:
Auth names an authenticator resource. When set, the principal is
resolved before dispatch and exposed to every node — so a node does not
have to re-derive identity, and an unauthenticated request never reaches
a graph that assumed one.

fields.doc:

names an authenticator, for endpoints like login that must be reachable
without credentials. It must be explicit: forgetting to set it fails
closed, forgetting to unset it does not silently open the route.

fields.doc:
Pick keeps only these keys (dotted paths allowed); Omit removes these.
When both are set Pick runs first.

fields.name: rename
fields.doc: Rename moves keys: rename { customer_id "customerId" }.

fields.name: coerce
fields.doc:
Coerce converts values in place: coerce { amount "float" age "int" }.
Supported targets are string, int, float, bool, time, duration, json.

fields.name: append
fields.doc: Append and Prepend concatenate onto an existing string or list value.

fields.name: flatten
fields.doc:
Flatten lifts the named nested objects' keys into the parent and removes
the nesting, e.g. flatten [address] turns address.city into city.

fields.name: redact
fields.doc:
Redact removes these paths entirely. Mask replaces them with a fixed
number of asterisks plus the last few characters, so a support agent can
still recognise a value without being able to read it.

fields.name: mask_keep
fields.doc: MaskKeep is how many trailing characters Mask preserves. Default 4.

block.doc:
DataTransformSpec is one per-path operation inside a DataSpec.

Either Expr (an expression whose result replaces the value at Path) or Op
(a named operation, optionally parameterised by Arg) must be set. Named ops
are the common cases that would otherwise need an awkward expression:
upper, lower, trim, title, slug, hash, base64, base64_decode, json_encode,
json_decode, round, abs, length, first, last, unique, sort, join, split,
now, timestamp, uuid, default.

fields.name: only_if
fields.doc:
OnlyIf gates the transform on an expression, so one spec can shape
conditionally without a branch node.

block.doc:
DataFilterSpec accepts or rejects a whole payload.

Mode is "allow" (the default: the payload proceeds only when Expr is true) or
"deny" (the payload is rejected when Expr is true). A filtered payload on an
intent boundary is an invalid-input failure; on a process edge it means the
edge does not traverse, which is how DAGFlow's filter edges behave.

fields.name: max_bytes
fields.doc:
MaxBytes and MaxDepth bound the payload after shaping. They are a real
safety limit, not a hint: exceeding either fails the boundary rather
than truncating, because silently truncated data is worse than a refusal.

fields.name: strict
fields.doc:
Strict rejects the payload when Extract or Transforms reference a path
that does not exist, instead of treating it as null. Turn it on for
anything whose correctness depends on the field being there.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc: Schema names a schema block validated against the final shape.

block.doc:
SecurityEventSpec reports this route's outcome to the document's
security.tcpguard resource (if one is declared), after the response is
known — OnSuccess when the final status is < 400, OnFailure otherwise.
Either may be left empty to report only one direction.

This exists because the guard's own automatic per-request check
(routes.go's serve, before dispatch) only ever sees "request.received":
at that point in the pipeline, whether a login attempt will succeed is
not yet decided. A rule keyed on an *outcome* — auth-abuse-velocity's
abuse.auth.ip_failures, account-takeover's session drift, anything
needing "did this attempt fail" — cannot fire without something telling
the guard that outcome after the fact, which is what this does.

	route "auth.login" {
	  ...
	  security_event { on_success "auth.login_success" on_failure "auth.login_failed" }
	}

schedule.name: schedule
schedule.doc:
ScheduleSpec runs an intent or a process on a recurring or one-shot
schedule. Schedules are enqueued onto a durable queue rather than run from an
in-process ticker, so exactly one replica executes each firing and a missed
window is not silently lost.

fields.name: every
fields.doc:
Every is a fixed interval; Cron is a 5-field crontab expression; At is a
single RFC3339 instant. Exactly one must be set.

fields.name: timezone
fields.doc:
Timezone names the IANA location a Cron expression is evaluated in.
Empty means UTC — never the host's local zone, which would make the same
configuration behave differently per machine.

fields.name: jitter
fields.doc:
Jitter spreads firings across replicas and avoids thundering herds on a
shared dependency. The delay added is uniform in [0, Jitter).

secret.name: secret
secret.doc:
SecretSpec resolves one named secret at load time, from the environment or a
file. A required secret that cannot be resolved fails compilation, so a
misconfigured deployment never starts serving — it refuses to boot.

Secret values are never included in the redacted Document that
Platform.Document exposes, and never logged.

shape.name: shape
shape.doc:
SchemaSpec is a reusable structural contract — a `shape` block — referenced by
validate.schema nodes, CRUD resources, human-task forms and route bodies.
One schema declared once is validated identically at every boundary.

fields.name: prop
fields.doc:
Props are the shape's fields. The block is spelled `prop` because BCL
reserves `field` for its own schema support and a block by that name never
binds.

block.doc:
SchemaFieldSpec is one property of a shape — a `prop` block. Kind is one of
string, int, number, bool, time, array, object, or the name of another shape.

fields.name: items
fields.doc: Items names the element type or schema for an array field.

fields.name: schema
fields.doc: Schema names another schema block for an object field.

fields.name: enum
fields.doc: Enum restricts the value to a fixed set.

fields.name: pattern
fields.doc: Pattern is a Go regular expression applied to string values.

fields.name: min
fields.doc: Min/Max bound numbers, and MinLength/MaxLength bound strings and arrays.

fields.name: format
fields.doc: Format applies a named string check: email, uuid, url, date, date_time.

fields.name: default
fields.doc: Default is substituted when the field is absent.

fields.name: sensitive
fields.doc: Sensitive fields are redacted from audit records and error messages.

fields.name: required
fields.doc:
Required lists field names required at this level, as an alternative to
marking each field. Both forms are honoured.

fields.name: additional_properties
fields.doc: AdditionalProperties defaults to true; set false to reject unknown keys.

static.name: static
static.doc: StaticSpec configures static file directory serving over HTTP.

tenant.name: tenant
tenant.doc:
TenantSpec declares one tenant of a multi-tenant deployment: its own limits,
its own constants, and the queues and processes it may use. An empty
allowlist means "no restriction", never "nothing allowed".

fields.name: region
fields.doc:
Region is the tenant's data home: a residency zone name or a region.
Writes on the tenant's behalf to a resource outside it are refused.

trigger.name: trigger
trigger.doc:
TriggerSpec is a non-HTTP-route entry point: an inbound webhook whose body
starts work, or a named event that resumes parked process runs.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc:
Kind is "webhook" or "event". BCL cannot bind a field named `type`, so the
discriminator is spelled `kind` here and everywhere else in this spec.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: Event is the process event name this trigger delivers, for type "event".

fields.name: secret
fields.doc:
Secret names a secret block holding the HMAC key for webhook signature
verification. A webhook trigger without one is rejected at compile time:
an unauthenticated public mutation entry point is never the intent.

fields.name: signature_header
fields.doc:
SignatureHeader and SignatureAlgorithm describe the incoming signature.
Defaults are "X-Signature" and "sha256".

fields.name: timestamp_header
fields.doc:
TimestampHeader and Tolerance bound replay. Zero tolerance disables the
timestamp check, which is only safe behind an idempotency guard.

fields.name: correlation_path
fields.doc:
CorrelationPath extracts the event correlation key from the body, e.g.
"order.id", so the event reaches the one run waiting for it.

worker.name: worker
worker.doc:
WorkerSpec binds a durable queue job type to an intent or a process.

Multiple process replicas may declare the same worker: the queue resource's
own Claim implementation owns the lease and atomic ownership, so exactly one
replica runs each job.

fields.name: process
fields.doc:
Process, when set instead of Intent, starts (or advances) a durable
process run from the job payload.

fields.name: concurrency
fields.doc:
Concurrency is a per-replica cap on simultaneous handlers for this job
type. Zero uses the queue resource's own worker count.

fields.name: max_attempts
fields.doc: MaxAttempts overrides the queue default for this job type.

fields.name: disabled
fields.doc:
Disabled keeps the declaration but stops consumption — the supported way
to drain a job type without editing every deployment.
